O.outcome_detail: monthly loan payment for a family of four with two dependent children and $81,000 AGI

cells.quote: An analysis of the RAP plan by The Institute for College Access and Success (TICAS) found a family of four with two dependent children and an adjusted gross income (AGI) of $81,000 would have a $440 payment under RAP but only a $36 payment the SAVE plan.
cells.note: Modeled policy comparison cited by the brief; no randomized comparison is reported.

cells.quote: Black borrowers — of whom 25.5% had a $0 payment (Table 2) — will be especially harmed by this.
cells.note: The table reports an observed race-group difference in EdTrust analysis of NCES Baccalaureate and Beyond data.

O.outcome_detail: percentage of graduate students versus percentage of Grad PLUS borrowers

result.effect: 46% of graduate students versus 68% of Grad PLUS borrowers

cells.quote: Graduate degree completers with incomes below $30,000 account for 46% of graduate students but 68% of Grad PLUS borrowers.
cells.note: The brief reports an observed group-composition difference; the comparison concerns representation among Grad PLUS borrowers.

O.outcome_detail: median cumulative months in economic-hardship or unemployment deferment four years after completing a bachelor’s degree

cells.quote: For borrowers who began college in 2016, four years after they completed their bachelor’s degree, the typical number of months on a financial hardship deferment was 12 (Table 4).
cells.note: The table reports race-specific medians, with Black or African American borrowers at 13 months and White borrowers at 12 months.
